newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritian rupee firms v dlr after intervention.
newsitem.headline: Mauritian rupee firms v dlr after intervention.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee firmed against both the dollar and sterling on Thursday with a central bank intervention on Wednesday seen supporting the local currency, forex dealers said.
The rupee traded at a mean commercial rate of 20.1015 rupees to the dollar on Thursday from 20.1465 on Wednesday.
Sterling was fixed at a mean rate of 33.1055 rupees, from 33.1250 on Wednesday.
Forex dealers said a late morning central bank intervention on Wednesday supported the rupee.
"The dollar was weaker in overnight international markets and if only this consideration is taken into account, the rupee would have gained one cent against the dollar," one dealer said.
"But because of the intervention of yesterday, the rupee has gained four cents on the dollar," the dealer added.
Sources at the central bank said $1.05 million were sold during Wednesday's intervention at 20.07 rupees to a dollar.
This was the second market intervention so far this week. The central bank sold $400,000 at 20.12 rupees on Monday.
Monday's intervention rate was again lower than the prevailing forex interbank rate, dealers said.
